name: Fabric mod
summary: A Fabric mod for Minecraft: Java Edition 26.x, built with Gradle and Fabric Loom.
description: A Gradle project in the shape of the official Fabric example mod for the unobfuscated 26.x versions: fabric.mod.json, a main entrypoint and, as options, a client entrypoint, a mixin, a command and an item. Needs JDK 25.

options.label: Mod name
options.patternHelp: start with a letter, at least two characters; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: The mod id is this name in lower case with underscores (My Mod becomes my_mod). The id names files and folders, so do not change it later.

options.label: Author
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: Goes into the Java package (com.author.modname) and the authors list.

options.label: Description
options.help: One line shown in the mod list.

options.label: Minecraft version
options.help: All three use the same project shape (no mappings, no remapping, Java 25). Older 1.21.x versions need a different build file and are not offered.

options.label: Fabric API version
options.help: Leave empty to use the build that goes with the Minecraft version above (0.165.2+26.3, 0.161.0+26.2 or 0.155.3+26.1.2). Newer builds are listed on fabricmc.net/develop.

options.label: Gradle version
options.help: The Gradle that the wrapper downloads. Loom needs a recent one.

options.label: Client entrypoint
options.help: A src/client source set with a ClientModInitializer, for rendering, screens and key binds.

options.label: Example mixin
options.help: A mixin into a game class, with its mixins json.

options.label: Example command
options.help: A slash command named after the mod id.

options.label: Example item
options.help: A registered item with its model, name and a place in the creative inventory.

next: Install JDK 25 if you do not have it. Minecraft 26.x mods cannot be built with anything older.
Open the folder in IntelliJ IDEA and let it import the Gradle project. From a terminal instead, run once: gradle wrapper
Test in a development game: gradlew runClient
Build the jar: gradlew build. It lands in build\libs.
Copy the jar (not the -sources one) to .minecraft\mods, next to Fabric API, and start the Fabric profile.
Look for the mod's loaded line in logs\latest.log. Your code starts in onInitialize in the main class.
